title: LG TV shown scanning LAN for third-party phones and other devices
gist: Packet-capture testing by Gamers Nexus and Level1Techs found that LG smart TVs natively scan the entire local network for unrelated devices and can capture microphone audio even while offline, undercutting LG's premium-brand reputation for lighter tracking and adding to its ad business's stated reach of 363 million 'addressable secondary devices' in the US.

insights.claim: Gamers Nexus, working with Level1Techs and security researchers, used Wireshark packet captures on LG TVs (including the pricey G5 OLED and the tested OLED65G3PUA, MSRP $2,500) and found the TVs scanning the entire local network, identifying dozens of unrelated devices such as staff smartwatches and phones that had no connection to the TV.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: This is independently verified packet-level evidence, not speculation, that a premium smart-TV brand is mapping entire home networks beyond its own device — a material privacy finding for any household or business using LG displays.
insights.quote: The [G5] crawled our entire network and found dozens of unrelated devices, including smartwatches and phones of our staff who didn’t even know we were working on this,

insights.claim: LG TV firmware analysis showed the devices are capable of identifying a user's IP address, geographic location, the names and signal strength of every nearby Wi-Fi network, channel numbers of neighboring Wi-Fi networks, and the internal IP addresses of other devices on the network even if those devices are never connected to the TV.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: The scope of data collected (geolocation, neighboring network mapping, unrelated device IPs) goes well beyond what's needed for basic device-connectivity or content-sharing features LG cites as justification.

insights.claim: Gamers Nexus editor-in-chief Steve Burke stated this scanning behavior is the TV's native, intended functionality and did not require exploiting any vulnerability.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Framing this as by-design rather than a bug means it cannot be patched away without LG changing product policy, making it a durable business-model issue rather than a one-off security flaw.
insights.quote: This is the TV’s native functionality. This didn’t require vulnerabilities,

insights.claim: LG's advertising division, LG Ad Solutions, has stated in recent marketing materials that it can reach 363 million 'addressable secondary devices' in the US.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: This figure quantifies the commercial scale of LG's device-tracking ambitions and suggests network-scanning capability plausibly supports ad-targeting infrastructure rather than only stated 'smart home' features.
insights.locator: LG's ad business, LG Ad Solutions

insights.claim: Testing demonstrated that an LG TV could capture microphone audio even while unplugged from the network, with the audio reportedly stored locally in plaintext, which could allow it to later be transmitted to LG if the TV reconnects online.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Plaintext local audio storage that persists across offline periods means the privacy risk doesn't end when a device is powered off or disconnected — a distinct and underappreciated exposure compared to simple 'is it listening right now' concerns.

insights.claim: LG's official response states that in standby mode the TV only monitors for a wake word if the user has previously enabled the 'Far-Field' feature, and that wake-word-detection audio is processed locally, promptly deleted, and not transmitted to LG servers unless voice functionality is intentionally activated.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: LG's rebuttal narrows the claim to a specific opt-in feature, but does not directly address the researchers' claim that captured audio was found stored locally in plaintext, leaving a gap between the two accounts.
insights.quote: When the TV is in standby mode and appears to be turned off, it only monitors for the wake word if you have previously enabled the Far-Field feature. If no wake word is detected, the audio used for wake word detection is processed locally on the TV, promptly deleted, and is not transmitted to LG servers.

insights.claim: Using an LG smart TV purely as a 'dumb monitor' does not necessarily stop all of the network-scanning and data-collection functionality described in the testing, according to Steve Burke.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: This undercuts a common consumer workaround (disabling smart features / using external inputs only) as a reliable privacy mitigation for LG TVs.
insights.locator: Burke pointed out that "even using an LG smart TV

insights.claim: Some ISPs, such as Comcast's Xfinity and AT&T, run dual-SSID setups that broadcast open neighborhood Wi-Fi hotspots from customers' routers, which devices can auto-connect to unknowingly (e.g., in apartment buildings), meaning the LAN-scanning risk described extends beyond LG specifically to smart TVs of any brand operating on such networks.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: This reframes the LG finding as a symptom of a wider systemic smart-TV/ISP privacy design problem rather than an LG-only issue, implying regulatory or industry-standard scrutiny could eventually target all smart TV makers, not just LG.
insights.locator: Internet service providers sometimes have dual SSIDs

insights.claim: LG has built a market reputation for fewer ads and less user tracking than budget TV brands, but that reputation is now under fresh scrutiny following this report and a separate prior revelation that LG monitors were installing McAfee ads onto connected Windows PCs.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: A premium brand's privacy-differentiation narrative eroding could affect consumer purchasing decisions and gives ammunition to critics pushing for smart-TV privacy regulation.
insights.locator: While this is a concern for all smart TV brands

insights.claim: The Gamers Nexus video also referenced remote code execution vulnerabilities in LG TVs that are currently going through the responsible disclosure process, separate from the by-design tracking behavior.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Undisclosed RCE vulnerabilities represent an additional, more acute security risk layered on top of the privacy concerns, worth monitoring once details become public.
